name: VOD To Plex
description: Dispatcharr plugin that bridges VOD movies and series into Plex via rclone HTTP mount with 302 redirect streaming, selective activation, and a Radarr/Sonarr-aware nightly auto-sync of your enabled VOD groups.
author: knmplace

fields.label: Dispatcharr
fields.description: Connection to Dispatcharr for VOD proxy streaming.

fields.label: Dispatcharr URL
fields.help_text: Full URL of Dispatcharr reachable by Plex (LAN IP, not localhost), including the port (e.g. http://192.168.1.x:9191). Used for 302 redirect playback and for resolving Dispatcharr's proxy redirects during audio probing — a URL missing its port will silently break both. Use 127.0.0.1 if running on same host.

fields.label: HTTP Server
fields.description: The plugin runs its own HTTP server for the dashboard UI and rclone/Plex streaming endpoint.

fields.label: Dashboard / Streaming Port
fields.help_text: Port for the web dashboard and VOD streaming endpoint. Must be exposed in Docker.

fields.label: Dashboard Host IP
fields.help_text: LAN IP of the Docker host (not the container). Used for dashboard URL and STRM file URLs.

fields.label: Auto-Start Server
fields.help_text: Starts the HTTP server automatically whenever this plugin is loaded — on container boot, Celery worker startup, and every time the Plugins page reloads plugins (which stops and reconstructs this plugin, and otherwise leaves the server down until Start Server is clicked again). Leave off to keep the current manual Start Server behavior.

fields.label: Plex Integration
fields.description: Connect to your Plex server to manage the VOD library and monitor playback.

fields.label: Plex URL
fields.help_text: Full URL of your Plex server (e.g. http://192.168.1.100:32400)

fields.label: Plex Token
fields.help_text: X-Plex-Token for authenticating with Plex API

fields.label: Plex Library Section ID (Movies)
fields.help_text: The Plex library section number for VOD movies (find via Plex API /library/sections). This may be your normal Movies library: add the rclone movies mount to it as an extra folder and set 'Plex path of the VOD movies mount' below.

fields.label: Plex Library Section ID (Series, auto-sync)
fields.help_text: Plex TV library that auto-synced episodes go into (may be your normal TV library). Auto-sync creates a Series Settings category 'Auto-sync' pointing at this section. 0 = no series auto-sync.

fields.label: Plex path of the VOD movies mount
fields.help_text: The folder of the rclone /vod/ mount as PLEX sees it (e.g. /mnt/vod/movies). Required when the VOD folder shares a Plex library with Radarr/Decypharr: Plex removals then only ever touch media under this path, and scans are limited to it. Without it, a Plex item that also holds a non-VOD file is never modified.

fields.label: Plex path of the VOD series mount
fields.help_text: The folder of the rclone /vod-series/ mount as PLEX sees it (e.g. /mnt/vod/series). Add <this path>/<category folder> (e.g. /mnt/vod/series/auto) to the Plex TV library. Same safety role as the movies path.

fields.label: Auto-sync series folder name
fields.help_text: Folder (under the series mount) auto-synced shows are written to. Fixed once the category exists.

fields.label: Add {tmdb-N} ids to names Plex sees
fields.help_text: Movie filenames and show folders get Plex's {tmdb-N} matching hint when Dispatcharr knows the TMDB id, so Plex matches the exact title and merges it with the same title from Radarr/Sonarr in a shared library. Applies to newly listed/created items.

fields.label: STRM Files
fields.description: Configure where STRM and NFO files are written for Plex to discover.

fields.label: STRM Output Directory
fields.help_text: Directory where .strm and .nfo files are written. Should be accessible to Plex via rclone mount or shared volume.

fields.label: Streaming
fields.description: Playback uses 302 redirect to Dispatcharr's native VOD proxy. No streaming configuration needed — Dispatcharr handles connections, Range requests, and session management.

fields.label: Debug: Log Connections & Server Errors
fields.help_text: Logs server start/stop errors and every connection to/from Dispatcharr and Plex (inbound VOD requests, outbound Plex API calls, redirect resolution) to the dashboard's Logs tab. Useful for diagnosing setup issues remotely. Generates a lot of log entries — leave off unless troubleshooting.

fields.label: Max Concurrent HEAD Probes (Plex Scan Throttle)
fields.help_text: During a Plex library scan, Plex fires many parallel HEAD/metadata probe requests at once (especially for series with lots of episodes). This caps how many the plugin processes at the same time — extra probes queue instead of all hitting your IPTV provider simultaneously, so a big scan or bulk activation doesn't blow past your provider's max concurrent connection limit. Lower it if your provider allows very few simultaneous connections; raise it if your provider tolerates more and you want scans to finish faster. Takes effect on next server start.

fields.label: Max Concurrent Connections Per Title
fields.help_text: Caps how many simultaneous real Dispatcharr VOD connections a single movie or episode can hold. rclone's VFS mount can re-open a file's stream several times over the course of one watch (not just a millisecond read-ahead burst) — each open is a separate real provider connection unless capped here. Extra sessions beyond the limit are force-dropped, keeping the most recently active ones, both when a new stream is requested AND on an ongoing ~10s background sweep (so connections opened outside the normal redirect flow, e.g. rclone re-hitting an already-issued redirect URL directly, still get caught). Set too high (or 0 to disable) relative to what your IPTV provider actually allows and you WILL hammer their concurrent-connection limit — most providers cap total simultaneous streams per account (commonly 1-3), and every activated title sharing that account competes for the same pool, so this should generally match or sit under your provider's per-account connection limit, not just what feels reasonable for one show.

fields.label: Only use enabled VOD groups
fields.help_text: Playback and activation only use provider streams from VOD groups (categories) you enabled on the M3U account in Dispatcharr, on active accounts, preferring the account with the highest VOD priority. Tip: turn off 'auto-enable new groups' on the M3U account so new provider groups don't switch themselves on.

fields.label: Streams kept free for viewers
fields.help_text: Background work (auto-sync batches, scheduled audio checks, Plex's first analysis of freshly auto-synced titles) never uses these last provider streams, counted over all active profiles of an account (Dispatcharr's max streams). Auto-sync pauses while fewer than this+1 streams are free.

fields.label: Auto-sync with Radarr / Sonarr
fields.description: Every night: bring in all movies/series from your enabled Dispatcharr VOD groups that Radarr/Sonarr don't have a file for, and remove the VOD copy of anything Radarr/Sonarr has since downloaded. Try 'Auto-sync: dry run' first.

fields.label: Radarr URL
fields.help_text: e.g. http://192.168.1.10:7878 (reachable from the Dispatcharr container)

fields.label: Max new movies per run
fields.help_text: Newest first. The rest follows on later nights.

fields.label: Max series episode lists fetched per run
fields.help_text: Dispatcharr only knows a series' episodes after fetching them from the provider (one API call per series, not a stream). New series first, then running shows.

fields.label: Pause between batches (seconds)
fields.help_text: Time for Plex to scan and analyze a batch before the next one lands.

fields.label: Audio-check each new movie
fields.help_text: Runs the ffprobe audio check per auto-synced movie. Costs one provider stream per title; off by default.

fields.label: Skip movies without TMDB/IMDb id
fields.help_text: Without an id the Radarr check can't work and Plex matching is guesswork.

fields.label: Also remove manually activated titles Radarr/Sonarr have
Treat 'in Radarr/Sonarr, no file yet' as owned
fields.help_text: Off: the VOD copy stays until the real file exists (VOD is the fallback). On: anything Radarr/Sonarr is looking for is kept out of the VOD library.

fields.label: Allow removing most auto-synced titles at once
fields.help_text: Safety valve: if more than half of the auto-synced titles suddenly look 'group disabled' (e.g. a provider refresh in progress), their removal is held back unless this is on.

fields.label: Security
fields.description: The dashboard/API and the rclone endpoints are open to anyone who can reach the port unless an access token is set.

fields.label: Access token
fields.help_text: Letters/digits. Dashboard: open http://host:port/?token=<token> once. rclone: add --http-headers "X-Bridge-Token,<token>" to both mounts. Requests from inside the Dispatcharr container are always allowed.

fields.label: Maintenance
fields.description: Background checks that keep the activated library in sync with Dispatcharr's VOD catalog.

fields.label: Removed-Movie Check Interval (seconds)
fields.help_text: How often the plugin checks whether activated movies still exist in Dispatcharr's catalog (e.g. after an M3U account refresh removes them). Cleans up orphaned STRM files and stale Plex entries. Minimum 10 seconds.

fields.label: Auto Stream Refresh Interval (days)
fields.help_text: How often each activated movie's cached provider pick is automatically cleared so the next play re-resolves fresh (light touch only — no STRM/Plex changes, movies currently playing are skipped). Set to 0 to disable. Use the dashboard's Refresh/Reactivate buttons for an on-demand or full fix.

fields.label: Untracked Orphan Sweep: Dry Run Only
fields.help_text: The reconcile cron also sweeps movie/series folders on disk that fell out of tracking (e.g. deactivated already, or predate STRM tracking) and are no longer in Dispatcharr's live catalog, removing their folder and matching Plex library entry. While this is ON, that sweep only logs what it WOULD remove (folder path + matched Plex entry) — nothing is actually deleted. Review the logged candidates, then uncheck this to let the sweep actually delete on its next cycle. No restart needed to take effect.

fields.label: Content Filtering
fields.description: Controls which categories are shown on the dashboard.

fields.label: Hide Adult Categories
fields.help_text: Excludes any category whose name contains "Adult" or "Adults" (e.g. 'Adult', 'FOR ADULTS', 'VOD Adults') from the dashboard's movie/series browse, category filters, and catalog summary. Uncheck to show adult categories again.

fields.label: Language Detection
fields.description: Optional. Enter a TMDB API key to enable looking up each movie's original language. Leave blank to disable this feature entirely.

fields.label: TMDB API Key (v3)
fields.help_text: TMDB v3 API key. Used for language lookups. Either this or the Read Access Token is required.

fields.label: TMDB Read Access Token
fields.help_text: TMDB API Read Access Token (Bearer). Takes priority over v3 API key if both are set.

actions.label: Open Dashboard
actions.description: Open the VOD To Plex web dashboard in a new tab.

actions.label: Start Server
actions.description: Start the HTTP server for the dashboard and streaming endpoint.

confirm.message: This will stop the dashboard and streaming endpoint. Active streams will be interrupted. Continue?

actions.label: Server Status
actions.description: Check the current status of the HTTP server.

actions.label: Auto-sync: dry run
actions.description: Compare your enabled VOD groups with Radarr/Sonarr and report what a sync would add and remove, without changing anything. Results appear in the dashboard's Auto-sync tab.

actions.label: Auto-sync: run now
actions.description: Run the auto-sync now instead of waiting for the nightly schedule.

confirm.message: This adds and removes VOD titles in Plex based on your enabled groups and Radarr/Sonarr. Run it now?
